_comment: Which demo acts have been recorded, and by when the unrecorded ones are owed. `docs/governance/demo-script.md` says 'the recordings ARE the deliverable' and `.claude/skills/close-milestone` step 8 says to record at close -- and NO act had ever been recorded. Act 0 belongs to M00b, which closed and tagged four milestones before this file existed. The rule was real, stated in two places, and enforced by nothing, which is this repository's most-repeated defect.
_why_this_is_data_and_not_prose: `brand_tone`'s widening was owed 'to M04' in an ADR, M04 closed without paying it, and nothing noticed. An obligation written only in a sentence is discharged by forgetting. `tests/test_demo_recordings.py` reads this file, so an act that goes unrecorded past the milestone it was deferred to turns the suite RED rather than turning invisible.
_what_recording_is_and_is_not_evidence_f: For Act 2 the EVIDENCE is PR #29 -- permanent, linkable, re-derivable by a stranger, carrying the gate's own posted comment and exit 1 in the workflow log. The claim in the twelve-claims table cites that PR, not a video, and nothing about claim 2's falsifiability depends on a recording. The recording is a PRESENTATION artifact. That is not true of every act -- Act 4's go/no-go artifact is produced BY the run -- so the distinction is recorded per act rather than assumed across all of them.
_why_deferred_from_exists: M05 is the first close where this file's teeth actually bit, and the milestone spent them: all three acts owed by M05 were re-deferred to M06. That is legal, deliberate and two-key -- and until ADR-049 it was also FREE and UNCOUNTED. `test_an_unrecorded_act_is_owed_to_a_milestone_that_has_not_closed` asks only whether the CURRENT `owed_by` has closed; it cannot tell a first deferral from a fourth, so an act could slide one milestone at a time forever, each slide green, each `why` rewritten to sound like the first. `deferred_from` is the ratchet: it lists every milestone this act was owed by and passed unrecorded, `tests/test_demo_recordings.py` derives it from the closed milestones rather than trusting it, and each one must be NAMED in `why`. A third slide therefore costs a visibly longer admission, in the file, signed by two seats. **M06 added the half that was missing: the ratchet now counts the milestone that just CLOSED, not only the one that OWNS the act.** Every assertion before it was satisfied by moving `owed_by` forward and leaving `deferred_from` alone -- the owner is already in the history after the first slide, the new `owed_by` is legitimately absent from it, and each listed milestone is still closed and still named in `why`. So `M06 -> M07` recording nothing was GREEN, and the count would have stayed at two while the truth was three. `uncounted_deferrals` derives the missing entry from the progression table: an unrecorded act whose owner is at or before the latest closed milestone passed that milestone, so it must be listed. `test_the_ratchet_fires_when_a_milestone_closes` runs it against a synthetic table where M06 is closed, because on the honest tree this guard cannot fire until the day it matters -- and a guard first exercised on that day is one nobody has run.
_what_the_m06_close_owes_this_file: WRITTEN BEFORE THE CLOSE, AND THE CLOSE WENT THE OTHER WAY. This field predicted that M06 would re-defer Acts 0, 1 and 2 to M07 -- three edits in one diff, two-key under ADR-049 -- and set out the arithmetic for doing it honestly. **The operator paid instead.** All three are recorded at `docs/governance/recordings/`, so `owed_by` stays at `M06` (it was owed by M06 and discharged by M06) and `deferred_from` keeps both slides rather than being cleared: the ratchet's job is to make a late payment visible as late, not to erase the debt once it is settled. The prediction is kept rather than deleted because a file whose whole thesis is that obligations must be counted should not quietly rewrite its own forecast when the forecast is beaten. What it got right is the mechanism: the moment the progression table marked M06 closed, `test_an_unrecorded_act_is_owed_to_a_milestone_that_has_not_closed` and `uncounted_deferrals` both went red and named all three acts, on the real tree, on the day it mattered -- which is what `test_the_ratchet_fires_when_a_milestone_closes` had asserted synthetically one PR earlier. The guard was not first exercised on the day it fired.

acts.title: The control
acts.why: Deferred twice now. M00b closed without it and the debt was invisible until M04 went looking; M05 accepted it, closed, and did not pay it either -- the operator's decision at the M05 close, taken deliberately rather than by forgetting, which is the whole difference this file exists to record. The arc argument is unchanged and is the reason all three move together rather than one being split off: Act 0's control hands its viewer context, evaluation clock and blackout table to ADV-010, and Act 2 is the platform blocking exactly that probe. Apart it is two clips. This act is also the only one of the three that cannot be recorded for free -- it needs live model calls against the ungoverned baseline -- and that cost is stated here rather than left as the unspoken reason. **PAID AT THE M06 CLOSE.** `deferred_from` keeps both slides: this was owed by M00b, re-deferred at M05, and recorded at M06 -- the history stays because the point of the ratchet is that a debt paid late is not a debt that was never owed. The take is live for beat 1 only: the control answers blackout-008 correctly and reports `source: entitlement-check`, a tool it does not have. Beats 2 and 3 read the committed M00b run and the published progression row, and the narration says so on camera rather than implying a live probe run.
acts.cost_to_record: live: AWS_PROFILE=agentpave, 25 goldens + 10 probes through services/highlights-agent-baseline/

acts.title: The paved road provides
acts.why: The reason this act carried until now -- 'Not yet buildable; M05 builds `pave new`' -- is FALSE as of PR 5 (#62) and is not restated. `python -m pave.cli new recap-agent` and `python -m pave.cli verify recap-agent` both run today, hermetically, at zero spend, and the verify failing on camera with its two findings is the beat the act is built around. So this is the first act in this file deferred past the milestone that OWNS it, and the reason is scheduling and not capability: the operator elected to record all three in one sitting at M06 rather than split the arc. Recorded plainly because a deferral whose stated reason has quietly expired is the exact failure `brand_tone` was. **PAID AT THE M06 CLOSE**, one milestone after the excuse above stopped being true. `pave new recap-agent` renders five files and `pave verify recap-agent` refuses it with two findings -- the registry grant and the twenty golden cases -- both on camera, failing, which is the beat that matters. The take also states what is NOT verified: there is no manifest verification at deploy, per ADR-046.
acts.cost_to_record: free: local CLI, no network, no model calls

acts.title: The gate decides
acts.why: Deferred twice now, M04 then M05. M04's evidence artifact exists and is stronger than a recording of it: PR #29, red for an L5 reason at exit 1, five probes named in the posted comment -- so deferring the video has still not deferred the proof, and claim 2 in the twelve-claims table cites the PR rather than a video. It moves with Acts 0 and 1 because of the ADV-010 thread they share, not because it is blocked on anything: this act costs nothing but a browser and three minutes. **PAID AT THE M06 CLOSE**, after two slides. Staged on the isolated exhibit commit `5a5a1aa` rather than PR #29's Files Changed -- the exhibit branch was cut before M04 merged, so the PR diff is 6546 lines across 28 files while the plant itself is six insertions in one file. The recording points at the placement, which is the whole defect: the plant returns PASS immediately above `if refused and logged:`, so G4's logged half is never consulted. It also says plainly that the comment reading `THE PLANT` would not exist in a real weakening, and that the gate caught this from the score, not the label.
